overview.text: The Gopher Snake (its eastern form is the Bullsnake) is a big, non-venomous snake of western and central North America. It is often mistaken for a rattlesnake, which it imitates when it is scared.

identification.text: Yellowish or sandy brown with a row of large dark brown or black blotches and smaller dark spots on the sides; the belly is yellowish. It has no rattle.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually about 91 to 213 cm (3 to 7 ft) long.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Western and central North America, from southern British Columbia, Alberta and Saskatchewan through the western and central United States to northern Mexico and Baja California.

behaviour.text: When threatened it puffs up, hisses, coils like a rattlesnake and shakes its tail; it often strikes with its mouth closed, just bumping with its nose to warn the attacker.

funfacts.text: Gopher snakes on islands with no rattlesnakes shake their tails for less time than those living alongside rattlesnakes.

recognise.text: Big blotched snake without a rattle.
Hisses loudly and copies a rattlesnake when scared.
